title: Disaster Collective Memory Role: fsQCA Causal Recipes for Preparedness Behavior
content: This study examines the role of disaster collective memory in promoting preparedness behavior using fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA). By analyzing earthquake cases in Mashiki (Kumamoto, Japan) and Palu (Central Sulawesi, Indonesia), along with each national-scope samples, this research evaluates configurations of five core conditions: collective memory, threat appraisal, coping appraisal, social norms, and trust. The analysis compares two distinct groups of causal recipes—one omitting collective memory and the other including it—to determine their paths to successful preparedness. The findings reveal that incorporating collective memory generates a perfect causal recipe, with Japan acting as the typical case. Concurrently, the model captures an efficacy-preparedness paradox within the Palu context. Methodologically, these results demonstrate that examining non-linear interactions between determinants provides significantly deeper insights than treating them as isolated factors in linear frameworks. This study highlights the necessity of designing highly contextualized disaster risk reduction strategies, emphasizing that a disaster case must be analyzed as a whole entity shaped by individual and social factors inherent to the affected region.
